data.jobspec:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=1
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --time=12:00:00
#   --mem=20GB

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=12h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=20GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

module load pytorch/1.4.0-py36-cuda90
module load torchvision/0.5.0-py36

python3 pvae/main.py --model mnist --manifold PoincareBall --c 0.1 --latent-dim 40 --hidden-dim 600 --prior WrappedNormal --posterior WrappedNormal --dec Geo --enc Wrapped --lr 5e-4 --epochs 80 --save-freq 80 --batch-size 128 --iwae-samples 5000

reasons: The original Slurm job required a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested 20GB of memory (`--mem=20GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.
